name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
vehicle: Falcon 9 Block 5 (booster B1085; rideshare with ispace's Hakuto-R Mission 2)
payload: Ten NASA instruments (about 94 kg together); lander launch mass 1,517 kg
first: Firefly's first Moon mission: it landed upright and worked for more than 14 days
description: Blue Ghost Mission 1 was Firefly Aerospace's first Moon mission, flown for NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services with ten NASA instruments. The lander, 2 m tall and 3.5 m wide, launched on a Falcon 9 on 2025-01-15 and spent about 25 days in Earth orbit, about four days on the lunar transit and about 16 days in lunar orbit. It entered lunar orbit on 2025-02-14. After a descent orbit insertion burn at 100 km on 2025-03-01, its powered descent began at 08:22 UTC on 2025-03-02, and it touched down at 08:34 UTC in Mare Crisium, near Mons Latreille, at 18.5623 N, 61.8103 E, within its 100 m landing target and upright. It worked for more than 14 days, took pictures of Earth eclipsing the Sun on 2025-03-14, and stopped after lunar sunset on 2025-03-16, having sent back more than 119 GB of data.

events.label: TRANS-LUNAR INJECTION
events.note: About 25 days in Earth orbit come before the lunar transit of about four days.

events.label: LUNAR ORBIT INSERTION
events.note: A 4 min 15 s burn on 2025-02-14, 01:51 UTC.

events.label: POWERED DESCENT
events.note: 2025-03-02, 08:22 UTC: a braking burn of about nine minutes.

events.label: TOUCHDOWN
events.note: 08:34 UTC in Mare Crisium, upright and within the 100 m target.

vehicle_stage: Falcon 9 second stage, to a highly elliptical Earth orbit
